topics.title: Getting started with MAGE
topics.summary: Choose your event and form, create a basic form when needed, then collect observations.

sections.title: Start with the right event
body: An event groups observations, forms, layers and people. Your account and event membership determine what you can view or change. An administrator may need to add you before an event appears.

Mobile clients and the web app share MAGE data, but their offline collection and location-sharing behavior is not identical. A downloaded guide works offline; it does not make remote maps, feeds or the web application work without a connection.
steps: Sign in using the authentication method configured for your installation.
Open the event selector in the top toolbar and select your assigned event.
Use the observation panel to open a record or select its marker on the map. Open an attachment to view the full file rather than only its preview.

sections.title: Choose a form before collecting an observation
body: Select a form linked to your chosen event before completing an observation. The form defines the questions, required answers and available attachment fields. A form from another event is not automatically available here.

If no suitable form is available, create a basic event form using the next section before proceeding. If you cannot access Administration or Create Form, ask an administrator or another authorized form manager to create it for this event; do not change to an unrelated event just to find a form.
steps: Confirm which event you are collecting for and which form the observation needs.

If a suitable form already exists, select it when the form picker appears after starting an observation, or choose Add Form in the observation editor. A form configured for every new observation is included automatically; confirm it is the correct one.
If the list is empty or the required form is missing, create a basic event form below, or ask an authorized administrator to do so, then return to the observation.

sections.title: Create a basic event form
body: Forms belong to events. Create the form on the same event in which observations will be collected. This setup requires form-management permission; users without it should ask an authorized administrator.

A basic form includes more than its questions: Map Symbology determines its appearance on the map, while Observation Feed determines which answers appear as the primary and secondary text in the observations list. The observation feed here is the list of observations, not an external data feed configured under Administration → Feeds.
steps: In Administration → Events, open the intended event and locate its Forms section.
Choose {{control:forms.new}}. Enter a clear Name, an optional Description and a Color.
Choose Add To Every New Observation when this form should be included automatically, then choose Next: Add Fields.

Add the fields you need, such as a Text field for a short report. Give each field a clear title and set Required Field where needed. Add an Attachment field if users will collect photos or files, and configure its allowed types and count limits.
Save the form and confirm it appears in this event's Forms list. Open the saved form to configure how its observations appear.

Expand Map Symbology. Start with the Default card and its pencil button to choose the map icon and configure the available line and fill appearance for observation geometries. Default provides the fallback appearance when no answer-specific symbol applies. A basic form does not need answer-specific symbols; mapping Select answers to different icons is covered in Advanced forms.

Expand Observation Feed. Choose a Primary Field for the main text shown in the observation list and a Secondary Field for supporting information. For example, use a report title as Primary Field and a status or short description as Secondary Field. No Primary Field or No Secondary Field leaves that text slot unassigned; it does not hide the observation. These choices do not change the map symbol, and are separate from similarly named fields under Map Symbology.

Check the sample observation-feed preview when available, then return to the map and create a test observation using this form. Enter sample answers and verify both the map symbol and the primary and secondary text in the observations list. When multiple forms are attached, their order also affects which form supplies the observation's leading presentation.

For further information on forms, open the Advanced forms chapter in this guide. It covers every field type, attachment options, Select-answer icon mappings, more detailed symbology and safe changes to existing forms.

sections.title: Create an observation
body: Create observations only in the intended event, using the form selected or created above. Coordinates, observation time, form values and attachments describe the record; check them before saving.
steps: Choose {{control:map.create}} on the map. Select the event-linked form in the picker, or confirm the automatically included form. Use Add Form if it is not yet attached. If no form is available, complete Create a basic event form above first.
Set the observation location and time, then complete the selected form's required answers. Open Location to move the marker or draw the relevant geometry, and save that location edit.
For photos or other files, use an Attachment field on the selected form. If that field is missing, ask an authorized administrator to configure it.

Save the observation and wait for saving and any attachment uploads to finish. Reopen the saved observation and its full-size attachment to confirm the result; do not navigate away while an upload is active.

sections.title: Find older or missing records
body: An empty list does not necessarily mean data was deleted. Event selection, time range, people, form and attachment filters can hide records. Browser preferences are local to that browser and origin; a restored installation on another port can start with different filters.
steps: In the Observations panel, choose {{control:map.filter}} and inspect the selected time range.
Select All in the Time field when you need older records; otherwise choose Custom, set a valid start and end time, and check the displayed timezone.
Apply the filter and check the event, people, form, favorites, important and attachment filter selections.
If records still fail to load, use Retry and check connection/error messages before recreating or deleting data.

sections.title: People, map layers and safe sign-out
body: The People view depends on event access and the location information teammates have actually shared. A missing location is not proof that a person is offline or at a particular place.
Use the map layer controls to select available backgrounds and overlays. Third-party imagery may require connectivity and its own access permissions.
steps: Choose the People view when you need teammate locations rather than observation records.
Check the age of location information before relying on it.
Finish saves and uploads, then use Logout when leaving a shared computer.

topics.title: Manage users: onboarding and offboarding
topics.summary: Provision accounts, assign appropriate access and remove access without treating deletion as the first step.

sections.title: Before you onboard someone
body: Use an existing administrator account with the required permissions. User roles and authentication options are installation-specific; do not assume a new account should be an administrator.
An account, a team membership and access to an event are separate concerns. Verify the complete path to the person's assigned event.
steps: Confirm the person's identity, approved role, authentication method and intended teams/events.
In Administration, open Users and search first to avoid duplicate accounts.

For administrator-created accounts, choose {{control:users.new}} and complete the required fields. Use a secure channel for initial credentials; do not put passwords in observation notes or guide downloads.

sections.title: Complete onboarding and verify access
body: Some deployments allow registration that requires activation or approval. Device registration can also be subject to administrator approval. Follow the controls your deployment actually exposes.
steps: Open the user details and review their active status, role and login configuration.
Assign approved team memberships and event access through the relevant team/event administration screens.
If a mobile device requires approval, review it in Devices before granting access.
Have the person sign in with their own account, select the intended event and confirm they can perform their assigned tasks without unnecessary privileges.

sections.title: Change access safely
body: Use the least privilege needed. Giving someone a team membership does not by itself justify granting system-wide administration. Keep at least one verified administrative recovery path.
steps: Review current role, teams, events, devices and logins before making changes.
Edit the user and the relevant memberships; save and reopen the records to verify the changes.
When you reduce access, verify it with a fresh sign-in rather than relying only on a previously open tab.

sections.title: Offboard without losing required records
body: Offboarding is a controlled access-removal process. Deleting an account is not equivalent to immediately revoking every existing session or identity-provider login, and it can affect record attribution. Retention and audit requirements take precedence.
Do not delete observations, attachments or shared event data merely because a user leaves.
steps: Confirm the offboarding request and required retention policy; preserve any required audit records.
Where supported, deactivate the account and remove unneeded team/event memberships.
Review registered devices and login credentials. For external authentication, also disable access at the identity provider and verify session-revocation behavior for your installation.
Verify denial of access using a fresh sign-in. Do not assume an already-issued token was revoked just because a membership changed.
Only use account deletion when authorized by policy after reviewing its consequences and backup/recovery requirements.

topics.title: Advanced forms
topics.summary: Configure every field type, attachment options and map symbols, then safely revise existing forms.
topics.audience: Form designers and event administrators; observation users

sections.title: Use a form and add attachments
body: A user needs a suitable form linked to the selected event before its attachment fields can be used. Naming a form in a guide does not attach it automatically to an existing observation.

Upload pending means MAGE has an attachment entry but not the file bytes. A pending entry cannot display the full photo. The original file is needed to resume an interrupted upload after the editor has been closed or refreshed.
steps: Create or edit an observation in the event that owns the form.
Add or select the form when it is not already included, and complete its required fields.

Use an attachment field to choose a supported photo or file, then Save. MAGE saves the observation and uploads the selected files even when a form is collapsed. Wait for saving and all uploads to finish before leaving.

If an upload fails while the editor is open, keep it open and Save again to retry the retained files. If you have already refreshed, edit the observation, expand its form, choose Select original file on the pending attachment and select the same original file with the same name, size and type. Save to resume on that attachment without creating a duplicate.

To discard a pending attachment instead, use its Delete attachment trash button while editing, then Save. It disappears from the editor immediately, but Cancel leaves the saved record unchanged. Deletion does not require uploading another file unless the field's required minimum would otherwise not be met. Adding a new attachment is separate from deleting the old one.
Reopen the observation and its full attachment to verify the file, not just a cached thumbnail.

sections.title: Design advanced fields and map symbols
body: The field editor supports multiple field types with type-specific options. Use choices for controlled vocabulary and suitable numeric/date fields when users need structured values. Requiredness and defaults should reflect real collection conditions.
Advanced form configuration can include field ordering, repeat behavior, map symbols and field-based symbol choices. Only configure options exposed for the selected field type.
steps: Design a simple example record and decide which fields are required, optional or repeatable.
Configure each field's choices, defaults and constraints, then order fields in a logical collection sequence.
Configure the available map/icon settings and verify each field-dependent icon choice with a test observation.
Test missing required values, unusual but valid values and multiple form entries before rollout.

sections.title: Text — short free-form answers
body: Text is a single-line answer for names, identifiers and short descriptions. It leaves the wording to the observer rather than limiting them to a predefined list. A default is a starting answer, not a restriction on what can be entered.
steps: In Form Fields choose Add Field, select Text, and enter a unique, meaningful Field Title.
Optionally enter Default Value and select Required Field when an answer must be supplied.
Add Field, save the form, then test an empty answer and an edited default on a training observation.

sections.title: Text Area — longer descriptions
body: Text Area provides multi-line free text for narratives, notes or detailed conditions. Use Select instead if consistent, predetermined answers matter more than an explanation.
steps: Choose Add Field → Text Area and name the information to collect.
Optionally enter a multi-line Default Value and enable Required Field.
Save and test a longer, multi-line answer in an observation.

sections.title: Number — measurements and counts
body: Number collects numeric values rather than text. Minimum Value and Maximum Value constrain the range; either can be left blank for no corresponding bound. Put units in the title, for example Water depth (cm), so users interpret the number consistently.
steps: Choose Add Field → Number and enter its title.
Set any minimum, maximum and default. Keep the default within the chosen range; choose Required Field if appropriate.
Save and test the boundaries, an out-of-range value and a decimal when the workflow needs one. A Number field is not a calculated field or an automatic counter.

sections.title: Email — email addresses
body: Email collects an email-address value with the observation form. It does not create a MAGE user, send an invitation or verify that the mailbox exists. Avoid collecting personal contact details unless needed for the event.
steps: Choose Add Field → Email and name the address being requested.
Optionally enter Default Value and enable Required Field.
Save and test address entry in a training observation; account onboarding remains a separate administration workflow.

sections.title: Date — dates and times
body: Date lets an observer enter a date/time for a named fact, such as an inspection time, in addition to the observation's own timestamp. The observation editor supplies date and time controls; pay attention to the displayed timezone. This field's configuration dialog does not offer an administrator-set default date.
steps: Choose Add Field → Date and give the date/time a clear Field Title.
Enable Required Field if appropriate, then add the field and save.
Enter a test value in an observation and reopen it to check the date, time and timezone.

sections.title: Checkbox — a true or false flag
body: Checkbox represents a checked or unchecked condition, such as Inspection performed. Its Default Value checkbox sets the initial state. It is not a list of mutually exclusive answers; use Radio Buttons or Select when the user needs to choose among named alternatives.
steps: Choose Add Field → Checkbox and use a title that clearly describes what checked means.
Choose the checked/unchecked Default Value and consider Required Field carefully.
Save and test both states. Do not use requiredness as a substitute for explaining whether unchecked is a valid answer or whether an explicit Yes/No choice is needed.

sections.title: Radio Buttons — one visible choice
body: Radio Buttons presents a short set of predetermined answers as visible alternatives, with one selection. It is useful for a small, stable vocabulary. The field dialog provides Field Options but no separate Default Value picker for Radio Buttons.
steps: Choose Add Field → Radio Buttons and enter the Field Title.
For each permitted answer, enter New option title and choose Add Option. Use the up/down controls to order answers and Delete option to remove an unwanted choice.
Choose Required Field as needed, save and test selecting each answer. For field-based map icons, use a single-answer Select field instead.

sections.title: Select — controlled answers and defaults
body: Select stores an answer from your predetermined Field Options rather than accepting arbitrary text. A single-answer Select is also eligible for value-based map symbology, so a chosen answer can select an icon other than the form's Default symbol. Merely adding an option does not assign its icon: configure Map Symbology separately.

Allow Multiple Selections changes the field to accept several answers. Single selection has a Default Value picker, including No Default; multiple selection has Default Values checkboxes. Recent Choices Limit promotes recently used answers to the top of the list; blank or 0 disables that feature. Multiple-selection fields are not offered as primary or variant map-symbol fields.
steps: Choose Add Field → Select and enter a meaningful Field Title.
Add each allowed answer using New option title → Add Option. Reorder or delete options as needed. For example, add Open and Closed to a Status field.
Decide whether to Allow Multiple Selections; configure its default answer or answers, Recent Choices Limit and Required Field.
Save and test every choice. Continue to Match Select answers to map icons when answers should change the map symbol.

sections.title: Location — additional mapped geometry
body: Location collects another geometry within the form, separate from the observation's main location. It is useful when the reported feature and an additional site or area need distinct positions. The observation geometry editor provides the supported drawing/location tools; the field dialog itself supplies a title and requiredness rather than numeric coordinates or a default geometry.
Location does not turn on Show Your Location or Report Your Location. Those map controls concern the device/user location, not a form answer.
steps: Choose Add Field → Location and name the extra location being requested.
Set Required Field if needed, add the field and save.
Create a training observation and use the location editor to set its geometry. Reopen the record to verify both the observation location and this additional geometry.

sections.title: Attachment — images, video, audio and other files
body: Attachment enables file collection in an event-linked form. Allowed Attachment Types exposes Image, Video and Audio; select one or several to allow those categories. If none are selected, the application explicitly warns that ANY file type is allowed. There is no separate Documents checkbox: leaving all categories unchecked permits other file types too.

Minimum Attachments and Maximum Attachments constrain the number of files on this field, not their size. Leave a bound blank for no corresponding limit. Attachment uses these count controls instead of the ordinary Required Field checkbox; use a minimum of 1 when at least one attachment is needed. Upload/file-size limits and what the browser or mobile client can capture or preview remain separate installation/client constraints.
steps: Choose Add Field → Attachment and enter a title such as Site evidence.
Choose the allowed categories: Image for photos/images, Video for clips, Audio for recordings, or a combination. Select none only when unrestricted file types are intended.
Set Minimum Attachments and Maximum Attachments if needed, with minimum no greater than maximum. Save the field and form.

In a training observation test an allowed file, a disallowed category when restrictions are set, and the count limits. Wait for upload completion, save, then reopen the full file; a thumbnail alone is not proof of a complete upload.

sections.title: User Select — event members
body: User Select is a dynamic list of users who are part of the event. Unlike Select, its options are not manually entered or deleted in Field Options; update event membership through the appropriate user/team administration workflow. Allow Multiple Selections enables assigning several event users instead of one.

Selecting a user records a form answer; it does not itself grant membership, send a notification or change permissions. A single-answer User Select is offered among eligible map-symbol fields, but its choices come from membership, not an administrator-maintained answer list.
steps: Choose Add Field → User Select and enter a Field Title such as Assigned reviewer.
Choose Allow Multiple Selections and Required Field as appropriate, then save.
Verify the available users with the event's membership and test one or multiple selections as configured.

sections.title: Match Select answers to map icons
body: Map Symbology is separate from the field dialog. Default supplies the form's base symbol; a primary answer can override it, and a second Variant Field can provide additional combinations. Eligible fields are active single-selection Select or User Select fields, not Text, Radio Buttons, attachments or multi-selection fields.

Each symbology entry can configure a Point Icon via Upload Icon, Line Color/Opacity/Width, and Fill Color/Opacity. Use a clearly recognizable icon for each meaning rather than relying only on color. Defaults for form answers and Default map symbology are different settings.
steps: Create and save a single-answer Select field, for example Status with Open and Closed choices.
Expand Map Symbology and choose Status as Primary Field. Keep a suitable Default symbol for records without a mapped answer.

Edit symbology for Open, choose Upload Icon and select its intended image. Repeat for Closed with a different icon; save the dialog and the map configuration. For line/polygon observations, configure the line and fill settings as needed.
Optionally choose a different eligible Variant Field and configure the answer combinations you need.
Create test observations for Open, Closed, no answer when allowed, and each configured variant. Reopen them and confirm the expected symbols on the MAGE map before using the form operationally.

sections.title: Edit existing forms safely
body: Changing a form can affect existing records and other administrators' drafts. Keep a backup and check the impact before removing fields or changing their meaning.
Coordinate edits with other administrators. Do not assume an open editor has the latest server definition or that every deployment offers conflict recovery.
steps: Review the current server form before editing. Keep the names/identifiers of existing fields unless a planned migration requires otherwise.
Retain important unsaved text before reloading to inspect a newer definition.
Review field order, required fields, choices and map/icon settings before saving. Check any errors rather than repeatedly submitting a stale draft.
Do not treat a missing icon preview as a successful upload. Verify each answer-specific symbol after saving.
Verify both an older observation and a new observation after publishing the revised form.

topics.title: Add and use layers
topics.summary: Configure imagery, static feature files and GeoPackages, then make them available to an event.
topics.audience: Administrators with layer permissions; map users

sections.title: Choose the right layer type
body: Imagery layers can use supported WMS, XYZ or TMS services. Feature layers support static geographic data such as KML/KMZ. GeoPackage layers provide a downloadable package; layer availability and mobile support depend on the package contents and client.
Check data licensing, coordinate coverage, access requirements and file size before uploading or sharing. Never place credentials in a public layer description.
steps: In Administration → Layers, choose {{control:layers.new}}.
Enter a descriptive name and choose the supported type that matches your source.
For imagery, configure the service URL and the available imagery options. For GeoPackage, select the .gpkg file. Static feature files are added through the feature-layer upload workflow.
Create the layer and review its details and any processing/error status before assigning it.

sections.title: Upload static features and verify processing
body: A successful file selection is not the same as successful server processing. Check the accepted format and limits shown by the upload control; not every ZIP is valid geographic data.
steps: Open the feature layer's details and choose an accepted KML, KMZ or ZIP file.
Keep the page open while uploading and inspect the upload result and layer processing status.
If processing fails, inspect the reported error and source file rather than repeatedly creating duplicate layers.
Verify the resulting features and bounds on the map.

sections.title: Make the layer available and use it
body: Creating a layer in the catalog does not necessarily make it available in every event. A remote imagery service can still fail when the browser or mobile client has no network access.
steps: Open the intended event in Administration and use its layer assignment controls to add the layer.
Return to the event's map, open the layer control and enable the desired background or overlay.
Check that features appear at the expected location and scale.
For offline work, prepare and test supported downloadable layers on the intended client before losing connectivity. Downloading this guide does not download the map data.

topics.title: Add and use feeds
topics.summary: Choose a feed service and topic, configure properties and preview content before event assignment.
topics.audience: Administrators with feed permissions; feed consumers

sections.title: Understand services, topics and feeds
body: A service supplies data and exposes topics. A feed selects a topic and configures its parameters, property schema, presentation and updates. Available service types can depend on installed plugins.
External data can be delayed, unavailable or subject to separate credentials and usage limits. Do not assume every item is current or that a feed is the same as an observation.
steps: Confirm the source, access requirements and desired topic with its owner.
In Administration → Feeds, choose {{control:feeds.new}}.
Choose an available service/topic, or use the service-creation step when your permissions and installed service types allow it.

sections.title: Configure and preview a feed
body: The editor proceeds through service/topic selection, topic parameters, item properties and feed configuration. Schema fields and required values depend on the chosen service.
Choose time and primary/secondary display properties from the properties actually returned by the source. Do not keep removed property names just because an older configuration used them.
steps: Provide the topic's requested parameters and proceed to the item-properties step.
Review the schema and available properties, then choose appropriate labels, time fields, icons and other display metadata.
Inspect the feed-item preview, including geometry and time values, before creating or updating the feed.
Save and reopen the feed to confirm the persisted configuration. If validation fails, correct the named fields rather than discarding the whole configuration.

sections.title: Assign, use and troubleshoot a feed
body: A feed may need event assignment before event users see it. An empty result can mean no matching source data, a time filter, a disabled feed or a failed request; it is not automatically a successful zero-item download.
steps: Open the intended event and add the feed through its feed-assignment controls.
Return to the event and review its feed content and available map display options.
Check the event, time range, source availability and any error messages if content is missing.
After changing a service schema or switching events, verify the displayed content belongs to the intended event and that property mappings still exist.

topics.title: Install and configure plugins
topics.summary: Separate server-side plugin installation from the configuration available inside MAGE.

sections.title: Know what requires a server operator
body: MAGE supports service and web-app plugins. The browser administration screen configures plugins that have already been installed and registered; it is not a general plugin marketplace or an upload-and-install tool.

Installing a plugin adds executable code to the server or browser. Only use trusted sources compatible with your exact MAGE version. Optional plugins are not automatically present in a private core Windows image.
steps: Identify the plugin, its trusted source, supported MAGE version, service/web components, configuration and external data requirements.
Review licensing, permissions, network access and secret-handling requirements.
Have the server operator back up the working deployment and test the plugin in a separate environment before changing the live installation.

sections.title: Install and register using the supported deployment
body: The upstream plugin contract requires a service init hook. The documented service launcher registers installed modules with repeated --plugin module-name arguments. Web plugins also require their web packages and application assembly configuration.

An instance package and a private Windows Docker deployment are different assemblies. Do not run generic installation commands inside a running container and assume those changes will survive replacement.
steps: Follow the chosen plugin's documentation to build/install its required packages in the controlled deployment source.
Register the installed service module in the deployment's startup configuration; upstream documents the mage.service --plugin mechanism.
For web functionality, include the plugin's web package and supported web assembly configuration, then rebuild the deployment as required.
Keep plugin/configuration changes separate from the upstream baseline and retain a rollback path. Never put secrets in a public Git branch or guide download.

sections.title: Configure in MAGE and verify
body: Only plugins that provide administration UI appear there. A plugin can be loaded without exposing an administrator page. Some plugins supply feed service types rather than a separate navigation page.
steps: Start the test deployment and inspect plugin initialization errors before opening it to users.
Sign in with an authorized administrator account and open the installed plugin's available navigation/configuration page.
Provide the plugin-specific settings through its documented mechanism. Verify an actual supported operation rather than just the presence of a menu item.
If the plugin supplies a feed service, continue with the Feeds guide and confirm the new service type is available.
Promote the tested deployment only after approval; preserve existing observations, resources and security files when replacing the application.
